corpus: 55 papers, 2,210 chunks (Qdrant Cloud, the public library)

featured.takeaway: Give a COVID-19 forecasting graph network a GraphCast-style multi-mesh, with edges reweighted by live mobility at each level, so disease-spread signals travel both locally (county to county) and over long range (between states).
featured.whyFeatured: Highest rating of the 24 cross-field runs (7.7, third of all 70) with low claim risk (0.15); four re-runs of the same request rated only 5.6 to 6.2.

featured.takeaway: Code-trained LLMs could grade programming assignments by functional correctness, as HumanEval scores code, but students could game weak unit tests the way search-generated programs do, so such graders need far stronger tests than instructors usually write.
featured.whyFeatured: Second-highest rating of the batch (7.6, fifth of 70); its claim sentence is one of only 3 of 110 the validator marked grounded (claim risk 0.15). Four re-runs rated 6.5 to 7.2.

featured.takeaway: Screenshot-to-code benchmarks such as Design2Code might be an early signal of job displacement for front-end engineers, but the validator flags as risky the claim that multimodal code generation explains the 28–40% of exposure variance older automation measures leave unexplained.
featured.whyFeatured: Shows the audit at work: no retrieved passage supports the cause the claim names, and the validator marks the sentence risky (0.75). Lowest rating of the batch (4.6).
